criteria.why: the layers that must not reach across a boundary cannot
every color in the product comes from a token in packages/theme
every guardrail catches the mistake it was made for
inline lint config, ts-expect-error and skipped tests are errors in the source tree
every rule in AGENTS.md names an enforcement path, and that path exists
a broken change fails before it reaches the branch
the merge gate runs the canonical commands and scores the harness
the procedure that turns a mistake into a permanent check is written down
mistakes are recorded in a shape a reader can scan
the repository is green on the commands a contributor runs

proofs.name: a workspace package imports the Tauri API

write.content:
import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";

export const probe = invoke;

proofs.name: a workspace package imports the desktop app

write.content:
import { App } from "../../../apps/desktop/src/App";

export const probe = App;

proofs.name: a workspace package imports the desktop app by its package name

write.content:
import { App } from "@arrow/desktop";

export const probe = App;

proofs.name: the source tree carries an inline lint config
the source tree carries a ts-expect-error
the source tree carries a skipped test
the source tree parses raw JSON
a component hardcodes a named color
the workspace ui alias resolves to its entry point

notes: The data-access criterion of the default harness was replaced. Arrow has no server-side data layer and no rows to own, so the criterion became the theme discipline: every color comes from a token in packages/theme.
The layer list is the Arrow layer list. The workspace packages under packages/ may not import the Tauri API and may not import the desktop app; the desktop app owns every Tauri call.
Raise minimumCriteria when a criterion is added. Never lower it to make the score pass.

minimumProofs is the floor on the proof set, and it lives here so the scorer and the prover cannot disagree about it. Raise it when a proof case is added. Never lower it to make the score pass, and never empty the proof set: a proof run that proves nothing fails.
The scorer counts the coverage check separately from the criteria, so a score of 10/10 means ten criteria passed.
